summary: Housing development is an allowed use on residential, mixed or commercial sites within 1/4 mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop (heavy rail or 72+ trains/day commuter rail) in an urban transit county (>15 passenger rail stations). Projects need at least 5 units and 30 du/acre. Applies to local agencies from July 1, 2026 (§ 65912.157(n)). The 75 ft / 120 du/ac figures are floors on local limits, not a unit cap. SB 79 does not by itself grant ministerial approval; see § 65912.159 for the streamlining path. Amended by SB 722 (Ch. 100, Stats. 2026, approved 2026-07-16) to exclude sites governed by the mobilehome and RV park laws.

summary: Municipalities must authorize multifamily and mixed-use residential in any area zoned commercial, industrial or mixed use, on property owned by a county, municipality or school district, and on religious-institution land of more than 3 acres (with a house of public worship for at least 10 years), regardless of the underlying zoning, if at least 40% of the residential units in a multifamily development are rentals affordable under s. 420.0004 for at least 30 years. No zoning change, special exception, variance or comprehensive plan amendment may be required for the height, zoning and density authorized. Density not below the highest allowed in the municipality; floor area ratio not below 150% of the highest allowed; height not below the tallest within 1 mile or three stories, whichever is higher; administrative approval. Parking must be cut 15% on request near transit and eliminated for mixed-use projects in a transit-oriented area. Counties have a parallel rule (s. 125.01055(7)). The subsection is listed to expire October 1, 2033. Qualifying units may receive the § 196.1978(3) property-tax exemption. Land that falls under one of the exclusions (airport-impacted areas, working waterfronts in industrial zones, the Wekiva and Everglades areas, open-character districts, areas of critical state concern, conservation easements) is outside the law.

parking_note: Municipality must reduce parking by 15% on request near a transit stop or other listed conditions, and must eliminate parking for mixed-use projects in a recognized TOD area (§ 166.04151(7)(f)).
